name: FlashMLA fused norm-RoPE-attention-RoPE-cast kernel: absorbing per-token scalar work into the attention kernel
arithmetic_intensity: This kernel changes nothing about the attention arithmetic; it removes kernels and bytes at the boundaries. It fuses Q-norm (V4 only, not V4.1), Q-RoPE, core attention, the conjugate O-RoPE and the cast of the output to FP8 into a single kernel. Each of those steps on its own is memory-bound elementwise work over the same tensors, so fusing them removes one HBM round trip per step and one kernel launch each. The stated cost is that Q_b and the Wv weights must be permuted in advance - i.e. the mechanism is paid for with an offline layout change, which is a real constraint because it makes the weight preparation model-specific. Author claim: the fused kernel still reaches the same or slightly higher TFlops while eliminating the small-kernel overhead, and the decode path of the fused kernel was optimized 10-15% in the 2026.09.30 release.
scales_with: hidden_width (elementwise norm/RoPE/cast cost is proportional to width, not to context)
batch_size (fewer launches matters most at small batch)
workarounds: Fuse every elementwise op that touches a tensor the attention kernel already has in registers
Pre-permute Q_b and Wv weights offline to make the fused RoPE register-friendly
Recommend the fused kernel over the standalone sparse prefill/decode kernels in DeepSeek's own testing
notes: Depends on TileLang, TileKernels and DeepGEMM to run the tests, i.e. it is a stack rather than a standalone kernel. CUDA only - Ascend is not supported for this kernel even though the sparse prefill/decode kernels are. This is the general 'kernel-boundary tax' pattern: at decode batch 1, several small elementwise kernels over hidden-dim tensors can cost as much in launch and round-trip overhead as the attention itself, and the fix is always fusion into whichever kernel already holds the tensor. Recorded as custom_kernel.
